subject: Ownership & traceability: data routing and subprocessor evidence request
messages:
From: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@arborhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@arborhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Ownership & traceability: data routing and subprocessor evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking a look at this. As part of our security and legal review for the pilot, we need a clear statement of how Redwood handles:

- whether tenant prompts/responses can be used for model improvement (we need a firm no-train or exact exclusions),
- how prompt/response ownership is documented, and
- routing decisions when a subprocessor (e.g., logging, analytics) is in a different region.

Specifically we need: a short operational statement we can include in our DPA annex, a list of subprocessors that might touch prompt/response data during handling, and any evidence you can share showing onshore routing or isolation for EU vs. US traffic.

Can you also confirm the guarantees for exportability of customer outputs (we want assurance our outputs are not used as model training data)?

Appreciate a checklist or example evidence pack we can share internally.

Best,
Samantha
Director, Security Operations
Arbor Health

--
Arbor Health is evaluating a restricted pilot and will need controls documented before pilot kickoff in late September.
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@arborhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@arborhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Ownership & traceability: data routing and subprocessor evidence request

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer up front: Redwood can commit to a no-training (no-model-improvement) operational mode for tenant traffic and provide an evidence pack showing routing/subprocessor boundaries.

What I'll do next:
- Attach our evidence checklist and a mapping of the known subprocessors and the data paths they touch. (See attached: redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf, subprocessor-routing-map.csv)
- Loop in our infra/security lead (Kimberly) to confirm the runtime routing options (onshore-only routes, EU residency toggles).
- Provide a short clause you can put in the DPA annex that reflects the operational controls and the no-training commitment.

Couple of clarifying Qs for your team before I prepare the DPA language:
1) Do you want proofs of routing for both production and any Dedicated/Private deployment options, or only for the hosted pilot?
2) For evidence, are you satisfied with system logs + signed attestation, or do you need periodic attestation + a copy of subprocessor contracts?

I can have a draft clause + evidence pack over by early next week.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0112

Attachment: redwood-evidence-checklist.pdf (Operational checklist, 6 pages)
Attachment: subprocessor-routing-map.csv (CSV, lists subprocessors, region, role)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 15:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Ownership & traceability: data routing and subprocessor evidence request

Hi Samantha — adding a bit of technical context so you can see what the evidence will show.

Operational guarantees we can provide for the hosted pilot:
- No-training mode: tenant traffic is processed on inference-only paths; telemetry used for runtime health is sampled and redacted and not included in model improvement pools. We will include a signed operational attestation to this effect.
- Routing: requests for EU-designated tenants can be routed to EU-hosted inference pools only; when routed to an onshore pool the KV/prefix cache is ephemeral and not persisted to global training stores.
- Subprocessors: the CSV lists logging, metrics, and SSO providers. For each we can provide scope statements showing they do not have access to aggregated training pipelines.
- Exportability: outputs (generated text) are customer-owned and can be exported on request; we maintain an export workflow and a transfer receipt which we will include in the evidence pack.

If you have specific legal wording you'd like us to mirror, paste it into a reply and we'll map the technical controls to each clause.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Infra Security, Redwood Inference

Samantha — attaching the final items for your review. Deliverables included:

- short DPA annex language (1 paragraph) you can paste into your DPA;
- evidence pack (signed runtime attestation + sample routing logs + subprocessor scope list);
- subprocessor-routing-map.csv (as discussed).

Summary of the DPA annex language (high level):
"Redwood Inference will not use customer-provided prompts or generated outputs for model improvement without explicit, documented consent. For the duration of the pilot, tenant traffic will be processed under the operational no-training mode; evidence of routing and subprocessor boundaries is available on request. Redwood will provide export support for generated outputs and periodic attestations concerning subprocessor access."

Next steps per our side:
- We will produce a signed attestation document (PDF) and a one-page technical note mapping controls to the DPA language.
- If Arbor wants subprocessor contracts, we can coordinate redacted copies after an NDA addendum (we typically supply scope-of-access excerpts rather than full contracts).

Please confirm you received the attachments and whether you want the DPA annex verbatim or with edits.

Best,
Grace
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
